Maya L: quick design review drop — uploaded Figma frames + a 45s walkthrough: https://figma.redwood/ux/1799812345 :eyes: Maya L: observed while clicking through the rules panel: - collapsed rules lose ordering cues; users ask 'which one is higher priority?' - drag handle only on hover; keyboard-only users can't reorder - preview simulation shows "Matched: default" when fallback kicks in, which is unhelpful - validation toast just says "invalid rules" with no context Jon R: re keyboard reorder: current rows are focusable but no explicit controls. Two options I prototyped: 1) small "Move up / Move down" icon buttons per row (visible on focus) 2) support keyboard drag via aria-grabbed + instructions in an aria-live region Jon R: ARIA snippet (rough): ```
Rule 2 — if user.agent contains "bot"
``` Priya S: visual affordance idea: add a subtle numeric badge left of the title (1,2,3) + faint vertical connecting line between collapsed items to imply flow. Keeps visuals light but communicates order. Priya S: validation copy suggestions: - specific single rule: "Rule 3: invalid expression — missing operator near '=='" - aggregated: "3 rules failed validation. Open rules editor to review." (make the second phrase a link) Sam T: preview should surface which rule matched + why. Proposed pill in preview: "Matched: Rule 3 (priority 1) — pattern 'beta' matched header.X-Flag". Click pill -> expand editor and highlight the matching condition. Sam T: also include simulated runtime values used for matching (e.g., request.headers.X-Region = "eu-west-1") so engineers can reproduce locally. Maya L: +1 on the preview pill. UX detail: when preview shows "default fallback" we should still show which earlier rules were evaluated and why they failed. Even a short list: "tested: Rule 1 (no match), Rule 2 (runtime error)" Jon R: implementation note: mapping preview match -> editor index needs stable rule IDs. We should emit telemetry event preview_match_opened with rule_id and preview_id so we can measure confusion hotspots. Priya S: accessibility nits: - drag handle must be keyboard focusable button with aria-label like "Move rule 2 up" and visible focus ring - use aria-live polite for validation errors so screen readers are notified without stealing focus - ensure color contrast on numeric badge and connecting line meets AA Maya L: microcopy options for preview pill/tooltips: - pill: "Matched: Rule 3 — click to inspect the matching condition" - tooltip: "Opens the rules editor and highlights the condition that matched this simulated request" Sam T: density control request: some customers have >50 rules. Propose a "Compact" toggle in the rules header that reduces row padding, hides secondary meta, and enables denser list virtualization. Priya S: if we add Move up/down buttons, ensure there is also an undo toast ("Moved Rule 3 up — Undo") so accidental changes are easy to revert. Toast should include an "Open changelog" link for audit. Designbot: snapshot 1799812345-uxshot uploaded to Figma review: https://figma.redwood/ux/1799812345-uxshot :white_check_mark: Maya L: next steps / owners: - Priya: iterate visuals + add numbered badge + compact toggle (ETA Wed) - Jon: prototype keyboard Move up/Move down + aria-live validation (ETA Thu) - Sam: add telemetry events (preview_match_opened, rule_move) and confirm preview payload includes runtime values (ETA Fri) - Maya: write QA checklist for preview->editor flow and validation messaging (ETA Mon) Sam T: I'll create follow-up tickets and link here. Thanks all :tada:
